title: Position is Power
content: Play more hands in late position (button and cutoff) and fewer hands in early position. Acting last gives you more information and control.

title: Tight is Right (Usually)
content: Play fewer, stronger hands. A common beginner mistake is playing too many hands. Start tight and loosen up as you improve.

title: Pot Odds Are Your Friend
content: Calculate pot odds to make mathematically sound decisions. If you need to call $10 into a $40 pot, you need 20% equity to break even.

title: Aggression Pays
content: Betting and raising is usually better than calling. You can win by making your opponent fold or by having the best hand at showdown.

title: Watch Your Opponents
content: Pay attention to betting patterns, timing tells, and opponent tendencies. Tight players rarely bluff, loose players call too often.

title: Bankroll Management
content: Never play with more than 5% of your bankroll at any single table. This protects you from going broke during bad runs.

title: Value Betting
content: When you have a strong hand, bet for value against weaker hands that might call. Size your bets to maximize profit from worse hands.

title: Bluffing Basics
content: Bluff against tight players and on scary boards. Avoid bluffing calling stations (loose-passive players) who rarely fold.

title: Continuation Betting
content: If you raised preflop, consider betting the flop (~70% of the time) even if you missed. Many opponents will fold weak hands.

title: Hand Reading
content: Try to put opponents on a range of hands, not just one specific hand. Consider their position, actions, and tendencies.

title: Never Fold When You Can Check
content: Checking costs nothing and preserves all equity. Folding when you could check is strictly dominated. If a coach ever tells you to fold for free, ignore it.

title: SPR Determines Plan
content: Stack-to-pot ratio (SPR) at the flop dictates strategy. SPR < 3: commit easily with top pair. SPR 4-10: play normally. SPR > 13: avoid stacking off without strong hands or nuts.

title: Block Bets
content: Small bets on later streets out of position can prevent opponents from making bigger bets you would have to call. They get more value but cost you less.

title: Use the Variance Graph
content: Realized winnings = EV + luck. Track all-in-adjusted winrate separately. A losing month at +5BB/100 EV is normal variance, not a strategy failure.

title: Don't Bluff a Calling Station
content: Loose-passive players call too much. Against them, increase value bets, decrease bluffs, and size up for thin value with marginal hands.

title: Three-Bet Polarized From the Blinds
content: Out of position 3-betting works best with a polarized range: premium value (QQ+, AK) plus suited connectors/Ax suited bluffs. Avoid 3-betting medium hands like JTo OOP.

title: Mind ICM at the Bubble
content: In tournaments near the money bubble, dollar EV diverges from chip EV. Chip-leader risk premium climbs — fold marginal jam/call spots that would be standard in cash.

title: Bet Sizing Matters More Than Bluff Frequency
content: Average players over-think frequencies and under-think sizing. Big bets polarize ranges; small bets cap them. Match your size to what your range needs to do.

title: Bayesian Sample Size Discipline
content: A 30% VPIP from 40 hands has a credible interval of roughly 18-44%. Don't fire 'too loose' flags until the CI excludes the target band. Small samples lie loudly.

title: Tilt Costs More Than Bad Luck
content: Bad beats are inevitable; tilting after them is a choice. Stop, breathe, and review the math: did you make the right decision regardless of outcome? Outcome bias is the silent killer.
